name: APT40
affiliation_detail:
On July 19, 2021, the DOJ unsealed a two-count indictment charging four individuals: three HSSD intelligence officers — Ding Xiaoyang (丁晓阳), Cheng Qingmin (程庆民), and Zhu Yunmin (朱允敏) — who coordinated, facilitated, and managed hackers and linguists at Hainan Xiandun and other MSS front companies; and Wu Shurong (吴淑荣), a hired hacker at Hainan Xiandun who created malware and conducted intrusions.
The anonymous research collective IntrusionTruth published two reports in January 2020 detailing the connections between Hainan Xiandun, APT40 activity, Ding Xiaoyang, and the Hainan MSS office — 18 months before the DOJ indictment confirmed their findings.
entity_name: Hainan Xiandun Technology Development Co., Ltd.
description:
According to U.S. DOJ indictment (2021) and Intrusion Truth (2020) investigation series, APT40 is a Chinese state-sponsored cyber espionage group attributed to the Ministry of State Security's Hainan State Security Department (HSSD), operating from Haikou, Hainan Province since at least 2009. 
The group conducted operations through the front company Hainan Xiandun Technology Development Company (海南仙盾). APT40's primary mission is the theft of intellectual property, and government intelligence in support of China's naval modernization, the Belt and Road Initiative, or high-tech R&D. (U.S. DOJ, 2021; FireEye, 2019)
According to the DOJ indictment, APT40 has targeted academia, aerospace, biomedical research, defense, government, healthcare, manufacturing, maritime technology, and transportation in 14 countries. Stolen information has included data on submersibles, autonomous vehicles, chemical formulas, commercial aircraft servicing, genetic-sequencing technology, and infectious-disease research. 
According to a 2024 CISA advisory, APT40 "possesses the capability to rapidly transform and adapt exploit proof-of-concept(s) (POCs)  of new vulnerabilities and immediately utilize them against target networks", often "within hours or days of public release."

campaigns.name: Naval Modernization and Maritime Espionage (TEMP.Periscope)
campaigns.description: FireEye documented APT40's campaign targeting maritime technology, naval research, engineering, and transportation sectors in support of China's naval modernization and blue-water navy ambitions. Targets included universities engaged in naval research, defense contractors, and organizations involved in submersible and autonomous vehicle development. The group masqueraded as an underwater vehicle manufacturer after China's PLAN seized a U.S. Navy UUV in the South China Sea in December 2016. Operations expanded to Belt and Road Initiative-related targeting across Cambodia, Belgium, Germany, the Philippines, Malaysia, Norway, Saudi Arabia, Switzerland, the U.S., and UK.

campaigns.name: Biomedical and IP Theft Campaign (DOJ Indictment)
campaigns.description: The DOJ indictment detailed APT40's theft of trade secrets and intellectual property from entities in 12 countries. Targeted information included data on submersibles, autonomous vehicles, chemical formulas, commercial aircraft servicing, genetic-sequencing technology, and infectious-disease research (Ebola, MERS, HIV/AIDS, Marburg, tularemia).

campaigns.name: New Zealand Parliamentary Breach
campaigns.description: New Zealand's GCSB/NCSC attributed a 2021 breach of the Parliamentary Counsel Office and Parliamentary Service to APT40. The compromise was detected relatively quickly and contained before strategic or sensitive data was exfiltrated. The attribution was disclosed publicly in March 2024 as part of a coordinated international action alongside the U.S./UK APT31 announcements.

campaigns.name: Australian Network Intrusions (ASD Case Studies)
campaigns.description: The 2024 multinational advisory documented two ASD-investigated breaches of Australian organizations in 2022. In the first case (July-September 2022), APT40 exploited a custom web application to establish a foothold in a network DMZ, then used compromised credentials for Active Directory enumeration and SMB-based data exfiltration. In the second case (April-May 2022), APT40 exploited RCE vulnerabilities in a remote access login portal, deploying web shells and capturing hundreds of username-password pairs, MFA codes, and JSON Web Tokens.
